title: The porcelain veneers procedure, step by step: how veneers are done
seoTitle: Porcelain Veneers Procedure: Step by Step
description: The veneer process from photos to bonding: design preview, 0.3 mm preparation, temporaries, lab day and delivery, and how long each step takes.
author: Dr. Roger Ramos Navarro, DMD
imageAlt: A patient in the treatment chair looking at her 3D smile design on a wall screen while the dentist points at it
answer: The porcelain veneers procedure has five steps: a **design you approve before any tooth is touched**, **about 0.3 mm of preparation** (sometimes none), temporaries in the approved shape, the lab making the veneers, and bonding. At most clinics that takes two to four weeks across several appointments. At Xiluet Smiles in Miami it takes **three visits in one week**, because the lab is in the building.

sections.h2: The veneer process at a glance

blocks.p: A veneer is a thin shell of ceramic bonded to the front of a tooth. Getting one is less an operation than a sequence of small, careful steps, and the order matters more than the drilling. The sequence below is the standard one described by the [American Dental Association](https://www.mouthhealthy.org/all-topics-a-z/veneers) and the [Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/23522-dental-veneers); the times are ours.

blocks.p: Two things decide how long the whole process takes: where the lab is, and whether the design is settled before the drill comes out. When the lab is across town, every step waits on a courier and the process stretches to two to four weeks. When the design is not approved first, the veneers come back from the lab and get adjusted in your mouth, which adds visits. Fix both and the procedure fits in a week.

sections.h2: Step 1: photos, a plan and a design you can see

blocks.p: The procedure starts before you sit in a chair. You send three photos of your smile from your phone, a doctor looks at them within 6 hours during office hours, and you get a written treatment plan: which teeth, veneer or crown per tooth, anything that needs treating first, and the total from the [published package prices](/veneers-cost-miami). Nothing is booked until that number is in writing.

Visit 1 is the exam and the design. We take X-rays, a professional cleaning, a 3D scan of your teeth and a set of photos and a short video of your face talking and smiling. From those, the new smile is drawn over your own face following your lip line, the width of your smile and the midline of your face. This is [digital smile design](/blog/what-is-digital-smile-design), and it is the step that decides whether the result looks like you or like a catalog.

You see the design on screen, and you can try it in your mouth as a mock-up before you approve it. Longer, shorter, squarer, softer: this is the moment to say so, because the ceramist works from exactly what you approve. Nothing is drilled at Visit 1.

blocks.quote: The design appointment is the most important two hours of the whole process. If a patient leaves it unsure, we do not prepare teeth the next day. We fix the design first.

sections.h2: Step 2: preparation, and why 0.3 mm is the number that matters

blocks.p: Preparation means smoothing a thin layer from the front of the tooth so the veneer sits flush instead of looking bulky. How much is removed is the single most important technical fact about your procedure, because enamel is about 1 mm thick on a front tooth and it does not grow back.

Conventional veneers are prepared to 0.5 to 0.7 mm, which usually stays in enamel. Our veneers are made at about 0.3 mm, so the preparation is about 0.3 mm and, on small or set-back teeth, sometimes none at all. The area is numbed first, enamel has no nerve endings, and most patients describe the visit as long rather than painful. [What each day feels like](/blog/do-veneers-hurt) is covered in its own article.

list: **Ask the number.** A practice should be able to tell you how much tooth it removes per veneer. If the answer is vague, or if the teeth in their before-and-after photos look like small pegs, that is a crown preparation, not a veneer.

**Ask what the veneer is bonded to.** Bonds to enamel last; bonds to dentin fail about [3.5 times more often](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jerd.70016). Staying at 0.3 mm keeps the bond on enamel.
**Ask whether the design guides the preparation.** When the ceramist already knows the final shape, the doctor removes only what that shape needs, tooth by tooth.

blocks.p: The difference between minimal preparation and the no-prep veneers sold under brand names is a question we get often enough that it has [its own article](/blog/minimal-prep-veneers-vs-no-prep-veneers). The short version: 0.3 mm is the amount that lets a veneer look natural without taking anything you will miss.

At the end of the preparation visit you leave with temporaries: a resin version of your approved design, made in your mouth from a mold of the mock-up. They do two jobs. They protect the prepared teeth, and they let you live with the new shape for two days: talk, smile in photos, eat a soft lunch, look at yourself in daylight rather than under a dental lamp.

Anything you would change goes to the ceramist before the porcelain is finished, not after. A millimeter off the length of the two front teeth, a slightly rounder corner: these are easy in the lab on Wednesday and impossible once the veneers are bonded on Thursday. Temporaries feel a little rough and look a shade flatter than porcelain. That is normal; they are a sketch of the final result, not the result.

sections.h2: Step 4: lab day, where the result is actually made

blocks.p: This is the step most patients never see and the one that decides whether the veneers look like teeth. From your scan and the approved design, each veneer is milled from a multilayer zirconia disc, then layered and finished by hand: the translucent edge, the subtle texture of the surface, the gradient from a warmer neck to a lighter edge that real enamel has. A set of 20 is a full day's work for a ceramist.

At most practices the lab is a company in another city, and the doctor meets the veneers for the first time at the bonding appointment. Ours is one floor above the treatment rooms, so the ceramist can walk down to look at your temporaries in your mouth, check the shade against your skin tone in daylight, and adjust before anything is fired. That is the practical reason the procedure takes a week here rather than a month, and the reason the Wednesday is yours: beach, Wynwood or rest.

sections.h2: Step 5: bonding and the final adjustments

steps: **Temporaries come off.** It feels odd rather than painful. The teeth are cleaned of any residue.

**Try-in.** Each veneer is placed with a water-soluble paste so you and the doctor can check fit, shape and shade together, in a mirror, before anything is permanent. The ceramist comes down for this.
**Isolation and etching.** The teeth are kept dry, lightly etched and primed so the cement bonds to enamel. This is the step that decides whether a veneer stays on for 15 years.
**Cementation.** A thin layer of resin cement, the veneer seated, excess removed, and a curing light sets it in seconds.
**Bite check.** You close and slide in every direction while the doctor marks and polishes any spot that hits first. A high spot is the main cause of a chipped veneer, so this is not rushed.
**Warranty and instructions.** You leave with the written 5-year warranty, a night guard appointment if you grind, and the aftercare sheet.

blocks.p: The bonding is final when you leave the chair. You can eat that day, carefully, and fly home that evening; most out-of-state patients do. Sensitivity to cold, if any, settles within a few days. The written warranty covers the veneer itself for five years, provided you keep up normal care and wear the night guard if one was prescribed.

sections.h2: How long the veneer procedure takes, start to finish

blocks.p: The week is the same whether you have one veneer or twenty, and the same for the 20-veneer [Smile Design](/smile-design-miami) at $5,999 and for [porcelain veneers](/porcelain-veneers-miami) on a few teeth at $1,000 each. If a tooth needs a crown instead of a veneer, or you need a deep cleaning first, it is on the plan and the estimate before you book. Full mouth cases take two weeks and are planned separately.

If you are flying in, the three visits fall on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, with the hotel, airport and packing details on the [out-of-state patients page](/out-of-state-patients). If you are local, the same three visits fit around a normal work week.

sections.h2: What to do before your procedure

list: **Send photos first.** Three photos from your phone through the [free photo evaluation](/free-photo-evaluation) get you a plan and a written total, with no visit.
**Whiten first if you plan to.** Veneers are matched to your natural teeth at the shade check, so finish whitening at least two weeks before Visit 1 and bring the shade you ended at.
**Fix gums and decay first.** Veneers go on healthy teeth. Deep cleaning or a filling, if needed, is on the plan before the design visit.
**Decide how you want to pay.** [Six financing partners](/financing) pre-qualify with a soft credit check; a $250 deposit, applied to your treatment, holds the three visits.
**Bring a night guard if you wear one,** and tell us if you grind. A guard after veneers is $400 and the best insurance the porcelain can have.

blocks.p: Then the procedure itself is what this article describes: a design you approve, a thin preparation, two days in temporaries, a day in the lab and a morning of bonding. Ask any clinic you are comparing to walk you through its version of the same five steps, with the numbers.

faq.q: How long does it take to get porcelain veneers?
faq.a: From first photos to bonded veneers, one week at Xiluet Smiles: the design visit on Monday, preparation and temporaries on Tuesday, lab work on Wednesday and delivery on Thursday. At clinics that ship to an outside lab, the same steps take two to four weeks across three to five appointments.

faq.q: How many appointments do veneers take?
faq.a: Three: exam and design, preparation with temporaries, and bonding. Some practices add a separate consultation and a try-in visit, which is why four or five appointments is also common. The number of teeth does not change the number of visits; 20 veneers and 2 veneers follow the same schedule.

faq.q: Do they shave your teeth down for veneers?
faq.a: A thin layer, not a shaving down. Conventional veneers remove 0.5 to 0.7 mm of enamel; ours are made at about 0.3 mm, so about 0.3 mm is prepared and on some teeth nothing at all. Teeth cut down to small pegs are crown preparations, not veneer preparations, and you should ask any clinic for its number.

The preparation visit is done under local anesthetic and most of the work stays in enamel, which has no nerve endings, so patients describe it as long rather than painful. Sensitivity to cold can appear for a day or two in temporaries and settles after bonding. The bonding visit itself does not hurt.

faq.q: Can I see what my veneers will look like before they are made?
faq.a: Yes, twice. At Visit 1 the design is shown on screen and tried in your mouth as a mock-up, and you approve it before any tooth is prepared. Then you wear temporaries in that shape for two days and can ask for changes before the porcelain is finished.

faq.q: What happens if I do not like my veneers at the bonding visit?
faq.a: The try-in exists for that: each veneer is placed with a removable paste first, and shape and shade are checked with you and the ceramist before cementation. Because the design was approved as a mock-up and lived with in temporaries, changes at this stage are rare and small, and the ceramist is one floor up if one is needed.
